            "content": "// The Signal Observatory draws the relationship hiding in a statement as a\n// figure between the statement's own words.\n//\n// This is the most machine-readable bank in the Centre, and the world leans on\n// that rather than on judgment. Measured across its 48 items:\n//\n// - All 48 credited answers parse as `type, \"indicator\"` groups, including the\n//   multi-relationship form (`conditional, \"Only if\"; causal, \"because\" and\n//   \"accelerates\"`).\n// - All 109 indicator words anchor to real words in their own statement, so\n//   every figure is drawn from text the student can see rather than from a\n//   position I chose. Three shapes of indicator needed handling to get there:\n//   a quote carrying a trailing period (\"lags.\"), a split comparative\n//   (\"more … than\"), and a separated pair (\"stronger than\" appearing as\n//   \"stronger ... than\").\n// - The authored relationship count agrees with the parsed group count on all\n//   48. Item 40 once declared four and listed three; the content was fixed, and\n//   the parse still follows the credited answer, because that is what the\n//   student is graded against.\n//\n// What this module does NOT do is decide which words are jargon. The Rung 4\n// dimming is still an open question on the drill's README and would need a\n// technical-vocabulary list nobody has written; dimming words by my own guess\n// at what looks technical would show a student my judgment as his teaching.\n\nimport type { ActivityItem } from \"../../api/types\";\n\nexport type RelationKind = \"conditional\" | \"causal\" | \"comparative\";\n\nexport interface Relation {\n  kind: RelationKind;\n  /** The indicator words as the bank quotes them. */\n  indicators: string[];\n  /**\n   * Where each indicator sits in the statement, as [start, end) offsets. A\n   * figure is drawn between these, so an indicator that cannot be found is\n   * never given a position.\n   */\n  anchors: { text: string; start: number; end: number }[];\n  /** Separated phrases (\"stronger ... than\") where every half must be quoted. */\n  requiredParts?: string[][];\n}\n\nexport interface Signal {\n  order: number;\n  rung: number;\n  statement: string;\n  relations: Relation[];\n  /** The count the bank declares in its own explanation, when it declares one. */\n  declared: number | null;\n}\n\nconst GROUP =\n  /(conditional|causal|comparative|comparison)\\s*,\\s*((?:\"[^\"]+\"(?:\\s+and\\s+)?)+)/gi;\nconst QUOTED = /\"([^\"]+)\"/g;\n\n/** Words too common to anchor a figure to on their own. */\nconst UNANCHORABLE = new Set([\"to\", \"the\", \"a\", \"an\", \"of\", \"in\", \"on\"]);\n\nfunction normalizeKind(raw: string): RelationKind {\n  const k = raw.toLowerCase();\n  // The bank writes \"comparative\"; the drill's badge says \"Comparison\". One\n  // name internally so the geometries table cannot drift from the parser.\n  return k === \"comparison\" ? \"comparative\" : (k as RelationKind);\n}\n\nfunction escape(text: string): string {\n  return text.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, \"\\\\$&\");\n}\n\nfunction locate(word: string, statement: string): { text: string; start: number; end: number } | null {\n  const m = statement.match(new RegExp(`\\\\b${escape(word)}\\\\b`, \"i\"));\n  if (!m || m.index === undefined) return null;\n  return { text: statement.slice(m.index, m.index + m[0].length), start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length };\n}\n\n/**\n * Where an indicator sits in its statement.\n *\n * Tried whole first, because \"only if\" is one indicator and should anchor as\n * one. When the whole phrase is not contiguous in the text, it is split: a\n * comparative like \"more … than\" is authored as a pair precisely because the\n * statement separates them, and the figure needs both ends.\n */\nexport function anchorsFor(indicator: string, statement: string) {\n  const whole = indicator.trim().replace(/[.,]+$/, \"\").trim();\n  const direct = locate(whole, statement);\n  if (direct) return [direct];\n\n  const out: { text: string; Anything not listed gets NO arrowhead: the shaft\n * still draws and still connects the two groups, it just makes no claim about\n * which way the rule runs.\n */\nconst DIRECTION: [RegExp, \"sufficient\" | \"necessary\"][] = [\n  // Necessary-condition markers first: \"only if\" must beat \"if\".\n  [/^only if$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^only when$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^only where$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^the only$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^requires?$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^required$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^depends on$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^contingent on$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^necessary$/i, \"necessary\"],\n  [/^if$/i, \"sufficient\"],\n  [/^when$/i, \"sufficient\"],\n  [/^whenever$/i, \"sufficient\"],\n  [/^wherever$/i, \"sufficient\"],\n  [/^where$/i, \"sufficient\"],\n  [/^provided$/i, \"sufficient\"],\n  [/^as long as$/i, \"sufficient\"],\n  [/^given$/i, \"sufficient\"],\n];\n\nexport function directionOf(indicator: string): \"sufficient\" | \"necessary\" | null {\n  const bare = indicator.trim().replace(/[.,]+$/, \"\");\n  for (const [re, dir] of DIRECTION) if (re.test(bare)) return dir;\n  return null;\n}\n\n/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *\n * Reading the student's answer\n * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */\n\nexport interface Reading {\n  /** Relationships the student named that are really there. */\n  found: RelationKind[];\n  /** Relationships they named that the statement does not carry. */\n  invented: RelationKind[];\n  /** Relationships in the statement they did not name. */\n  missed: RelationKind[];\n  /** True when they also quoted at least one credited indicator per found type. */\n  quotedIndicators: boolean;\n  /**\n   * A figure is drawn only for a relation the student both named AND is real.\n   * A named-but-absent type draws as a ghost that dissolves.\n   */\n  drawn: RelationKind[];\n}\n\n/**\n * The words a student uses to name each type. (!NEGATED_BEFORE.test(before)) named.add(kind);\n    }\n  }\n  return named;\n}\n\n/**\n * Read a free-text answer in the drill's game format (\"conditional, only if\").\n *\n * The type is what gets ------------------------------------------------------------------ */\n\n/** Lowercase, straight quotes gone, \"only-if\" read as \"only if\". */\nfunction normalize(text: string): string {\n  return .split(/…|\\.\\.\\./)\n    .map((p) => p.trim())\n    .filter(Boolean);\n  if (!parts.length) return false;\n  return parts.every((part) => {\n    const re = new RegExp(`\\\\b${escape(part)}\\\\b`, Overview\n\n**Creative North Star: \"LSAT Academy\"**\n\nOne institution with two registers, and the seam between them is deliberate.\n\n**The Hall** is the door. It is the only place in the product where atmosphere outranks throughput.\n\n**The Workroom** is everything past sign-in. Light, neutral, and quiet, because a student sits inside it for an hour reading dense argument text and the interface must not compete with the passage. There is no warmth here and that is the decision, not an oversight: warm accents need a dark ground to read, and on the Workroom's white they collapse. The Hall's bronze measures 8.58:1 on its own night and 2.30:1 on the Workroom's page. The two registers do not share a palette because they cannot.\n\nWhat they do share is restraint about meaning. In both, colour is a signal. Green, red and amber say something happened. Nothing is coloured to be warm, to look premium, or to fill a space. Depth comes from hairlines and background tone rather than shadow, and hierarchy comes from size, weight and position rather than hue.\n\nInside the Workroom, individual rooms may commit fully to their own world. The eight Activity Centre worlds, the scoped bootcamps and the inbox each carry a painted identity behind a wrapper class. That is sanctioned and it is what an academy is: neutral corridors, characterful rooms. The corridor never takes on a room's paint.\n\n**Key Characteristics:**\n- Two registers, one institution: a dark marble Hall at the door, a light neutral Workroom inside.\n- Colour means something or it is absent.\n- Flat surfaces, hairline separation, no drop shadows.\n- Precise and quiet controls that stay out of the reader's way.\n- Rooms may be worlds; corridors never are.\n\n## Colors\n\nTwo grounds, one shared vocabulary of meaning.\n\n### Primary\n\n- **Workroom Ink** (`#121212`): the Workroom's near-black. It is the text colour, the fill of every primary button, and the colour of the focus ring. The Workroom has no accent, so ink carries emphasis by itself.\n- **Hall Bronze** (`#c6a467`): the Hall's warm light. Hairline borders on the call to action, a sheen across it on hover, and the selection highlight. It exists only on the Hall's night ground and never crosses into the Workroom.\n\n### Secondary\n\n- **Hall Cyan** (`#8ad8e2`): the Hall's cool instrument note against the bronze, and the colour of its focus outlines. Rare by design; it marks precision where bronze marks warmth.\n- **Teacher Amber** (`#c7841f`): the single accent of the teacher workspace, with a hue-locked ramp for hover (`#af7318`), text on tinted fills (`#895910`) and a light step (`#e0a648`). Deliberately theme-independent: the workspace is always the light format. It is the one accent in the product, and it belongs to the operator, not the student.\n\n### Tertiary\n\nIndividual rooms carry their own palettes behind a wrapper class and are documented in their own surface briefs, not here. The wrappers in use are `.classroom-root`, `.mc-bootcamp`, `.ff-bootcamp`, `.rc-bootcamp`, `.topic-abstract`, `.cs-punk`, and the eight Activity Centre worlds.\n\n`.classroom-root` was added to this list on 2026-09-08, after an audit found the classroom running on Outfit and a warm palette while this record still described it as neutral Workroom chrome. It is a sanctioned world, not drift: the warmth and the typeface are deliberate and they are what makes the classroom feel like a study rather than a dashboard. The record was wrong, not the code. Its brief is `.impeccable/surfaces/classroom.md`. Note that this is the one sanctioned world that is also a corridor, so the rule below about corridors never being worlds now has exactly one documented exception.\n\n### Neutral\n\n- **Workroom Page** (`#fcfcfc`) and **Card** (`#ffffff`): the page ground and the surface that sits on it. One step of separation, no more.\n- **Workroom Raised** (`#f7f7f7`) and **Fill** (`#f2f2f2`): the two tonal steps available for layering and for resting fills.\n- **Workroom Ink Muted** (`#737373`): secondary text. Measures 4.62:1 on the page, which clears the floor with almost nothing to spare. Do not lighten it.\n- **Workroom Hairline** (`#e0e0e0`) and **Field** (`#e6e6e6`): the borders that do the work shadows used to.\n- **Hall Marble** (`#eae5da`), with secondary (`#a6a093`) and muted (`#6e695e`) steps: warm off-white text on the night ground.\n\n### State (semantic only, never decorative)\n\n- **Correct** (`#10b77f`) and **Incorrect** (`#f43e5c`): a student's attempt was right or wrong. Held under their own names, separate from system status, so a future shift to one cannot silently reframe the other.\n- **Warn** (`#f59f0a`): a bonus, a stretch, a non-blocking notice.\n- **Success** (`#21c45d`), **Warning** (`#f59f0a`), **Destructive** (`#dc2828`): system status, not student performance.\n\n### Named Rules\n\n**The Ground Decides Rule.** A warm colour is legible on the Hall's night and illegible on the Workroom's page. Never carry a colour across the seam on the strength of liking it; measure it against the ground it will land on first.\n\n**The Meaning-Only Rule.** A colour appears in the Workroom because something is right, wrong, cautionary, or dangerous. There is no fifth reason. If a surface feels flat and the impulse is to add a colour, the answer is type and space.\n\n**The Named Ground Rule.** No colour is written as a literal hex in a component. It resolves from a token, and a token that resolves to nothing is a defect, not a subtle effect. Three colour names in this codebase pointed at variables that were never defined, and the product silently lost its focus ring for five months.\n\n## Typography\n\n**Workroom Body:** Lexend (with Outfit, then the system stack)\n**Hall Display:** Fraunces (with Iowan Old Style, Times New Roman, serif)\n**Hall Inscription:** Cinzel (with Trajan Pro, serif)\n**Mono:** IBM Plex Mono\n**Question Lock:** Outfit, held deliberately for LSAT question surfaces\n\n**Character:** The Workroom is one humanist sans doing everything, sized and weighted rather than swapped. The Hall is a serif institution: an optical serif for its headings and an inscriptional face for its few carved lines. The split is the whole typographic idea. Inside, type gets out of the way; at the door, type is the architecture.\n\n### Hierarchy\n\n- **Title** (600, 24px, line-height 1, tracking -0.025em): card and section headings in the Workroom.\n- **Body** (400, 14px rising to 16px at 640px and above, line-height 1.6): everything a student reads in the Workroom chrome.\n- **Question** (400, 16px, line-height 1.6, Outfit): LSAT stimulus and answer choices. Font-locked to Outfit even though the rest of the app moved to Lexend, so question text does not shift when the shell's face changes.\n- **Label** (500, 14px): button and control labels.\n- **Hall Display** (380, fluid, tracking -0.015em, Fraunces): Hall headings. The unusually light 380 weight is the point; it reads as carved rather than printed.\n- **Hall Inscription** (500, tracking 0.05em, Cinzel): the Hall's few short carved lines. Never body copy.\n- **Hall Mono** (400, 13px, tracking 0.04em, IBM Plex Mono): the Hall's instrument labels.\n\n### Named Rules\n\n**The One Face Rule.** The Workroom uses a single family. Hierarchy is built from size, weight and space. A second family inside the Workroom is a defect unless it is the Outfit question lock.\n\n**The Question Never Moves Rule.** LSAT question text is font-locked. A change to the shell's typeface must not reflow a passage a student is mid-way through reading.\n\n**The Serif Stays At The Door Rule.** Fraunces and Cinzel belong to the Hall. A serif appearing in the Workroom chrome means the seam has leaked.\n\n## Layout\n\nThe Workroom is a centred single column with generous side gutters. The container centres by default, carries 32px of horizontal padding, and stops widening at 1400px.\n\nBreakpoints are the framework defaults up to 1280px, with the largest step pulled in to 1400px. Body type steps from 14px to 16px at 640px, and form controls are forced to 16px below 768px so that iOS does not zoom the page when a field takes focus. Named breakpoints `phone` (up to 600px), `tablet` (601 to 900px) and `desktop` (901px and up) exist for bootcamp surfaces.\n\nSpacing runs on a 4px base. The steps in real use are 4, 8, 16, 24 and 32. Card padding is 24px on all sides; button padding is 8px vertical and 16px horizontal.\n\nReading measure matters more here than in most products. Passage and stimulus text is held to a comfortable line length rather than allowed to run the full container width.\n\n### Named Rules\n\n**The Reading Measure Rule.** Any surface carrying an LSAT passage, stimulus, or explanation constrains its own line length. The container's maximum is a ceiling for layout, never a licence for prose.\n\n## Elevation & Depth\n\n**Flat, with hairline separation.** Surfaces sit on the page rather than above it. A card is distinguished from its ground by a one-pixel border and, where more is needed, by one step of background tone. There are no drop shadows in the Workroom.\n\nThis is a decision, not a description. The codebase currently ships five shadow tokens tuned for a dark ground, from `0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` up to `0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.7)`, and applies the smallest of them to every card. Because the app ships light by default, those shadows land at 40 percent black under a white card. The light theme never redefined them, and the one glow token is white, so it is invisible on white. The tokens are retired by this record and the code has not caught up yet.\n\nThe Hall is the exception and keeps its own depth: fixed ambience gradients, a grain overlay, and an inset highlight on its call to action. That depth is atmospheric rather than structural, and it does not transfer.\n\n### Named Rules\n\n**The Flat Rule.** Depth in the Workroom comes from a hairline or a tonal step. A `box-shadow` on a Workroom surface is a defect.\n\n**The Two-Step Rule.** Page, then card, then at most one raised step. A surface that needs a fourth level of layering is a surface that needs restructuring.\n\n## Shapes\n\nCorners are gently rounded and consistent: 8px for cards and containers, 6px for buttons and inputs, 4px for the smallest chips and insets, and a full pill only for genuine badges. The scale derives from one 0.5rem radius token, so a change to the base moves the whole system together.\n\nThe Hall uses a near-square 2px radius instead. Its edges are cut, not softened, which is what separates a carved surface from a card.\n\nBorders are one pixel. There is no second border weight in the Workroom.\n\n### Named Rules\n\n**The Hairline Rule.** One pixel, always. A thicker border used as a coloured accent stripe on the leading edge of a surface is banned, including when faked with an inset shadow. Active state is carried by background tone.\n\n## Components\n\n### Buttons\n\n- **Character:** precise and quiet. A button is a plain rectangle with a label. It darkens slightly on hover and does nothing else. It does not lift, does not cast a shadow, and does not scale on press.\n- **Shape:** gently rounded (6px).\n- **Primary:** ink fill (`#121212`), page-coloured label, 8px by 16px padding.\n- **Outline:** page background, one-pixel field border, ink label.\n- **Ghost:** no fill at rest, a tonal fill on hover.\n- **Sizes:** default 44px tall, small 40px, large 48px, icon 44 by 44. Every size clears the 44px touch minimum by being that height, never by relying on wrapped text or padding accidents.\n- **Focus:** a solid two-pixel ink outline, offset two pixels from the edge. This is the only focus treatment in the Workroom.\n- **Hall CTA:** 60px tall, near-square corners, transparent fill over a bronze hairline, with a bronze sheen that sweeps across on hover and a cyan outline on focus.\n\n### Cards / Containers\n\n- **Corner:** 8px.\n- **Background:** card white on the page ground.\n- **Border:** one-pixel hairline. This is what separates the card, not a shadow.\n- **Shadow:** none.\n- **Padding:** 24px, with header, content and footer sharing that inset.\n\n### Inputs / Fields\n\n- **Style:** page background, one-pixel field border, 6px corners, 44px minimum height, 8px by 12px padding.\n- **Focus:** the same two-pixel ink outline as buttons, offset two pixels. Do not express focus as a border colour change alone; a border shift is too quiet to serve as the only indicator.\n- **Mobile:** 16px text below 768px, so focusing a field never zooms the viewport.\n\n### Navigation\n\nNeutral chrome throughout. The sidebar runs one tonal step off the page ground with a hairline edge, and the active item is marked by background tone rather than by a coloured rule on its leading edge.\n\n### Signature Component: the scoped world\n\nThe product's distinctive pattern is not a control, it is a container. A room commits fully to its own palette, typefaces and atmosphere behind a single wrapper class, and nothing inside it leaks out. Scene layers are `aria-hidden` furniture painted beneath the content, so the accessible tree is identical whether the room is painted or bare. A new world is added by writing a new wrapper and its prefixed tokens, never by adding hex to a shared component.\n\n## Do's and Don'ts\n\n### Activity entries must make the next action clear\n\nReading Center correction, 2026-10-16: Joshua rejected competing emphasis, repeated summaries and unclear tutorial labels on LR Recall. An activity entry serves someone choosing work or learning how to do it. It must not require them to read a promotional landing page first.\n\n- Give the main task one dominant action. Keep instructions and examples clearly available as a secondary destination. A control's label must describe what it actually does: choosing a section, starting a new attempt and opening a report are different actions. Never label a new attempt Resume.\n- Each section must help the student act, understand a requirement or inspect their own work. Remove a repeated explanation instead of finding a new slogan for it. Product-name chips, headings and taglines do not each need to repeat the same name or method.\n- Use explicit teaching labels, such as Instructions and Video examples. Numbered demonstration selectors use Example 1, Example 2 and Example 3; source citations are secondary metadata. Accessible names must agree with the visible labels.\n- Keep the four steps and recorded examples within the same activity area, using clearly labelled views where appropriate. Keep necessary detail available without repeating the same step body in several adjacent components. Long explanations should be optional once the task and requirements are clear.\n- Shorten presentation without dropping the method: silent reading, looking away, retelling aloud in one's own words, reacting and recalling the complete argument remain distinct requirements. Do not infer understanding from delivery alone or promise improvement on an unsupported timetable.\n- Preserve a scoped room's approved visual identity, but make decorative motion subordinate to the task and the actual tutorial. Do not introduce another competing demonstration merely to fill a hero.\n\nThese are reusable review constraints. Joshua approved the LR Recall replacement layout after the clarification interview on 2026-10-16. The dated Reading Center correction in [.impeccable/surfaces/src-features-activity-centre.md](.impeccable/surfaces/src-features-activity-centre.md) records its scope. Approval does not establish publication; that requires separate live verification. Palette, runner behavior, grading and saved work are unchanged by this document.\n\n### Drill creation and drill history are separate destinations\n\nRC correction, 2026-10-15: selecting **Create** opens the passage builder directly. Existing sittings belong in **In progress** or **Completed**, filtered by the selected LR/RC section. Do not put an attempt list, results, or Resume/Delete controls under Create, or add a second Create button merely to reach setup. Preserve the preview-to-start boundary: a preview reads the selected content; starting creates the sitting. Assigned work and protected timed sections keep their own destinations.\n\nThe RC builder uses Workroom semantic tokens on its entire setup surface. Its inherited dark-card palette must not place pale text on a light card. Check both themes, selected controls, keyboard focus, phone, mid-width, wide and docked layouts in the rendered app. Saved-set copy must state its actual support: reusable templates currently support LR, while RC sittings are in history. These are scoped corrections and implementation constraints, not approval of exact replacement copy or a mandate to copy another platform's layout.\n\n### Spot practice must make the task and completion clear (2026-10-16)\n\n- Omit keyboard-shortcut helper copy beneath answer inputs by default. Retain keyboard submission, navigation, visible focus and accessible controls.\n- Use ordinary student labels: Sentence and Your answer. Keep internal metaphors, Rung and difficulty categories out of task and feedback UI. Authoring and parser metadata may remain internal; the scoped visual identity does not require metaphorical task labels.\n- Ask the learner to name each relationship and quote the words that signal it. Each answer needs a relationship type and supporting quotation, including every type present in a sentence.\n- Drive the accessible completion bar from resolved questions, separately from question position and accuracy. Entering question 48 with 47 resolved means 47 of 48 completed, not 100%. Only resolution of the final question earns full completion. Revealed or deliberately unjudged completion does not establish correctness or mastery. Expose a meaningful name, range/current value and completed-count text; do not rely on color alone and honor reduced motion.\n- Give a response-specific hint before revealing a first unsuccessful answer. Retain the learner's text and useful hint during retry. Correct responses receive the full authored explanation. Explicit reveal or the existing attempt cap shows the full answer and explanation; the illustration agrees with the shown answer while the earned verdict stays unchanged. Keep full answers and explanations hidden during the first unresolved unsuccessful attempt. Unavailable grading remains honestly unjudged.\n- Place feedback and the full explanation before Next or Finish in reading and keyboard order. Once the question resolves and an authored explanation is available, suppress advice to retry it; preserve the earned verdict.\n- Normalize the exact legacy fallback at the presentation boundary to: Check that each relationship type matches the words you quoted. Reread the whole sentence for any relationship you missed. Do not bring rejected words-create-it wording back through fallback feedback. Keep other grader feedback and all verdicts intact; a presentation correction must not rewrite historical responses, grading keys or earned results.\n\nVerification covers initial, correct, wrong, editing retry, reveal and unavailable states; completion at zero, resume, last unanswered and final resolution; keyboard/screen-reader access, visible focus, computed contrast, reduced motion and narrow/mid-width/wide/docked layouts. Check semantic judgments and teaching feedback separately, including the exact legacy fallback and explanation-before-Next order. See [.impeccable/surfaces/src-features-activity-centre.md](.impeccable/surfaces/src-features-activity-centre.md) for surface-specific behavior. The vault's wiki/COPY-CORRECTIONS.md and bootcamp-builder teaching-preference ledgers retain dated correction history.\n\n### Do:\n\n- **Do** resolve every colour from a token, and treat a token that resolves to nothing as a defect. Verify a new token renders before documenting it.\n- **Do** give every interactive element a visible focus indicator: a solid two-pixel ink outline offset two pixels in the Workroom, cyan in the Hall.\n- **Do** check contrast against the ground the colour will actually land on, in the theme that actually ships, in a browser. The theme file has read as correct while the page rendered a light card on a near-black ground.\n- **Do** separate surfaces with a one-pixel hairline and one tonal step.\n- **Do** keep colour semantic: correct, incorrect, warning, danger. Nothing else earns it.\n- **Do** scope a new room's identity behind its own wrapper class with prefixed tokens, the way the bootcamps and the eight Activity worlds already do.\n- **Do** hold LSAT passage and stimulus text to a readable line length, and leave it on the Outfit question lock.\n- **Do** end every world's stylesheet with a `prefers-reduced-motion` block that stops continuous motion rather than speeding it up.\n\n### Don't:\n\n- **Don't** add a `box-shadow` to a Workroom surface. Depth is hairline and tone.\n- **Don't** carry a Hall colour into the Workroom. Bronze reads 8.58:1 on the Hall's night and 2.30:1 on the Workroom's page.\n- **Don't** introduce a warm or metallic accent into the Workroom to make it feel premium. Premium here is depth, hierarchy and type.\n- **Don't** remove the browser's focus outline without shipping a replacement in the same rule. `outline-none` with no working ring is worse than leaving the default alone.\n- **Don't** animate the focus indicator. A `transition-all` on a control means the ring fades in, which delays the one signal a keyboard user depends on.\n- **Don't** use a border thicker than one pixel as a coloured accent stripe, including when faked with an inset shadow.\n- **Don't** put a second typeface into the Workroom chrome, and don't let a serif cross in from the Hall.\n- **Don't** animate layout properties. Animate `opacity`, `transform` and `color`. No bounce, no elastic, no lift on hover.\n- **Don't** write a hex value into a component. If a room needs its own colour, promote it to named tokens behind that room's wrapper.\n\n<!--\nKnown gaps between this record and the code, as of 2026-09-05. Above, not\n          below: below is where the letters are. */}\n      {kind === \"causal\"\n        ? shapes.map(({ d }, n) => (\n            <path\n              key={`echo-${n}`}\n              className=\"ob-figure\"\n              data-kind=\"causal\"\n              d={d}\n              transform=\"translate(0,-3)\"\n              opacity={0.6}\n            />\n          ))\n        : null}\n      {/* Comparative gets a level beam under each stretch that spans two terms.\n          Level, because the figure does not know which term is greater, and an\n          \"as strong as\" has no greater term at all. */}\n      {kind === \"comparative\"\n        ? shapes\n            .filter(({ seg }) => seg.count > 1)\n            .map(({ seg, base }, n) => (\n              <g key={`beam-${n}`} className=\"ob-beam\" data-testid=\"ob-beam\">\n                <line className=\"ob-figure\" data-kind=\"comparative\" x1={seg.x1} y1={base} x2={seg.x2} y2={base} />\n              </g>\n            ))\n        : null}\n      {showHead ? Design System: LSAT Academy\n136: \n137: ## Overview\n138: \n139: **Creative North Star: \"LSAT Academy\"**\n140: \n141: One institution with two registers, and the seam between them is deliberate.\n142: \n143: **The Hall** is the door. Unauthenticated, dark, and material: near-black ground, warm marble text, a bronze that carries the light, and a serif that behaves like carved lettering. Its own source calls it a museum nocturne, carved marble filmed in darkness, read by modern instruments. Its job is to make a prospective student feel they are entering somewhere, not signing up for something. It is the only place in the product where atmosphere outranks throughput.\n144: \n145: **The Workroom** is everything past sign-in. Light, neutral, and quiet, because a student sits inside it for an hour reading dense argument text and the interface must not compete with the passage. There is no warmth here and that is the decision, not an oversight: warm accents need a dark ground to read, and on the Workroom's white they collapse. The Hall's bronze measures 8.58:1 on its own night and 2.30:1 on the Workroom's page. The two registers do not share a palette because they cannot.\n146: \n147: What they do share is restraint about meaning. In both, colour is a signal. Green, red and amber say something happened. Nothing is coloured to be warm, to look premium, or to fill a space. Depth comes from hairlines and background tone rather than shadow, and hierarchy comes from size, weight and position rather than hue.\n148: \n149: Inside the Workroom, individual rooms may commit fully to their own world. The eight Activity Centre worlds, the scoped bootcamps and the inbox each carry a painted identity behind a wrapper class. That is sanctioned and it is what an academy is: neutral corridors, characterful rooms. The corridor never takes on a room's paint.\n150: \n151: **Key Characteristics:**\n152: - Two registers, one institution: a dark marble Hall at the door, a light neutral Workroom inside.\n153: - Colour means something or it is absent.\n154: - Flat surfaces, hairline separation, no drop shadows.\n155: - Precise and quiet controls that stay out of the reader's way.\n156: - Rooms may be worlds; corridors never are.\n157: \n158: ## Colors\n159: \n160: Two grounds, one shared vocabulary of meaning.\n161: \n162: ### Primary\n163: \n164: - **Workroom Ink** (`#121212`): the Workroom's near-black. It is the text colour, the fill of every primary button, and the colour of the focus ring. The Workroom has no accent, so ink carries emphasis by itself.\n165: - **Hall Bronze** (`#c6a467`): the Hall's warm light. Hairline borders on the call to action, a sheen across it on hover, and the selection highlight. It exists only on the Hall's night ground and never crosses into the Workroom.\n166: \n167: ### Secondary\n168: \n169: - **Hall Cyan** (`#8ad8e2`): the Hall's cool instrument note against the bronze, and the colour of its focus outlines. Rare by design; it marks precision where bronze marks warmth.\n170: - **Teacher Amber** (`#c7841f`): the single accent of the teacher workspace, with a hue-locked ramp for hover (`#af7318`), text on tinted fills (`#895910`) and a light step (`#e0a648`). Deliberately theme-independent: the workspace is always the light format. It is the one accent in the product, and it belongs to the operator, not the student.\n171: \n172: ### Tertiary\n173: \n174: Individual rooms carry their own palettes behind a wrapper class and are documented in their own surface briefs, not here. The wrappers in use are `.classroom-root`, `.mc-bootcamp`, `.ff-bootcamp`, `.rc-bootcamp`, `.topic-abstract`, `.cs-punk`, and the eight Activity Centre worlds.\n175: \n176: `.classroom-root` was added to this list on 2026-09-08, after an audit found the classroom running on Outfit and a warm palette while this record still described it as neutral Workroom chrome. It is a sanctioned world, not drift: the warmth and the typeface are deliberate and they are what makes the classroom feel like a study rather than a dashboard. The record was wrong, not the code. Its brief is `.impeccable/surfaces/classroom.md`. Note that this is the one sanctioned world that is also a corridor, so the rule below about corridors never being worlds now has exactly one documented exception.\n177: \n178: ### Neutral\n179: \n180: - **Workroom Page** (`#fcfcfc`) and **Card** (`#ffffff`): the page ground and the surface that sits on it. One step of separation, no more.\n181: - **Workroom Raised** (`#f7f7f7`) and **Fill** (`#f2f2f2`): the two tonal steps available for layering and for resting fills.\n182: - **Workroom Ink Muted** (`#737373`): secondary text. Measures 4.62:1 on the page, which clears the floor with almost nothing to spare. Do not lighten it.\n183: - **Workroom Hairline** (`#e0e0e0`) and **Field** (`#e6e6e6`): the borders that do the work shadows used to.\n184: - **Hall Marble** (`#eae5da`), with secondary (`#a6a093`) and muted (`#6e695e`) steps: warm off-white text on the night ground.\n185: \n186: ### State (semantic only, never decorative)\n187: \n188: - **Correct** (`#10b77f`) and **Incorrect** (`#f43e5c`): a student's attempt was right or wrong. Held under their own names, separate from system status, so a future shift to one cannot silently reframe the other.\n189: - **Warn** (`#f59f0a`): a bonus, a stretch, a non-blocking notice.\n190: - **Success** (`#21c45d`), **Warning** (`#f59f0a`), **Destructive** (`#dc2828`): system status, not student performance.\n191: \n192: ### Named Rules\n193: \n194: **The Ground Decides Rule.** A warm colour is legible on the Hall's night and illegible on the Workroom's page. Never carry a colour across the seam on the strength of liking it; measure it against the ground it will land on first.\n195: \n196: **The Meaning-Only Rule.** A colour appears in the Workroom because something is right, wrong, cautionary, or dangerous. There is no fifth reason. If a surface feels flat and the impulse is to add a colour, the answer is type and space.\n197: \n198: **The Named Ground Rule.** No colour is written as a literal hex in a component. It resolves from a token, and a token that resolves to nothing is a defect, not a subtle effect. Three colour names in this codebase pointed at variables that were never defined, and the product silently lost its focus ring for five months.\n199: \n200: ## Typography\n201: \n202: **Workroom Body:** Lexend (with Outfit, then the system stack)\n203: **Hall Display:** Fraunces (with Iowan Old Style, Times New Roman, serif)\n204: **Hall Inscription:** Cinzel (with Trajan Pro, serif)\n205: **Mono:** IBM Plex Mono\n206: **Question Lock:** Outfit, held deliberately for LSAT question surfaces\n207: \n208: **Character:** The Workroom is one humanist sans doing everything, sized and weighted rather than swapped. The Hall is a serif institution: an optical serif for its headings and an inscriptional face for its few carved lines. The split is the whole typographic idea. Inside, type gets out of the way; at the door, type is the architecture.\n209: \n210: ### Hierarchy\n211: \n212: - **Title** (600, 24px, line-height 1, tracking -0.025em): card and section headings in the Workroom.\n213: - **Body** (400, 14px rising to 16px at 640px and above, line-height 1.6): everything a student reads in the Workroom chrome.\n214: - **Question** (400, 16px, line-height 1.6, Outfit): LSAT stimulus and answer choices. Font-locked to Outfit even though the rest of the app moved to Lexend, so question text does not shift when the shell's face changes.\n215: - **Label** (500, 14px): button and control labels.\n216: - **Hall Display** (380, fluid, tracking -0.015em, Fraunces): Hall headings. The unusually light 380 weight is the point; it reads as carved rather than printed.\n217: - **Hall Inscription** (500, tracking 0.05em, Cinzel): the Hall's few short carved lines. Never body copy.\n218: - **Hall Mono** (400, 13px, tracking 0.04em, IBM Plex Mono): the Hall's instrument labels.\n219: \n220: ### Named Rules\n221: \n222: **The One Face Rule.** The Workroom uses a single family. Hierarchy is built from size, weight and space. A second family inside the Workroom is a defect unless it is the Outfit question lock.\n223: \n224: **The Question Never Moves Rule.** LSAT question text is font-locked. A change to the shell's typeface must not reflow a passage a student is mid-way through reading.\n225: \n226: **The Serif Stays At The Door Rule.** Fraunces and Cinzel belong to the Hall. A serif appearing in the Workroom chrome means the seam has leaked.\n227: \n228: ## Layout\n229: \n230: The Workroom is a centred single column with generous side gutters. The container centres by default, carries 32px of horizontal padding, and stops widening at 1400px.\n231: \n232: Breakpoints are the framework defaults up to 1280px, with the largest step pulled in to 1400px. Body type steps from 14px to 16px at 640px, and form controls are forced to 16px below 768px so that iOS does not zoom the page when a field takes focus. Named breakpoints `phone` (up to 600px), `tablet` (601 to 900px) and `desktop` (901px and up) exist for bootcamp surfaces.\n233: \n234: Spacing runs on a 4px base. The steps in real use are 4, 8, 16, 24 and 32. Card padding is 24px on all sides; button padding is 8px vertical and 16px horizontal.\n235: \n236: Reading measure matters more here than in most products. Passage and stimulus text is held to a comfortable line length rather than allowed to run the full container width.\n237: \n238: ### Named Rules\n239: \n240: **The Reading Measure Rule.** Any surface carrying an LSAT passage, stimulus, or explanation constrains its own line length. The container's maximum is a ceiling for layout, never a licence for prose.\n241: \n242: ## Elevation & Depth\n243: \n244: **Flat, with hairline separation.** Surfaces sit on the page rather than above it. A card is distinguished from its ground by a one-pixel border and, where more is needed, by one step of background tone. There are no drop shadows in the Workroom.\n245: \n246: This is a decision, not a description. The codebase currently ships five shadow tokens tuned for a dark ground, from `0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` up to `0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.7)`, and applies the smallest of them to every card. Because the app ships light by default, those shadows land at 40 percent black under a white card. The light theme never redefined them, and the one glow token is white, so it is invisible on white. The tokens are retired by this record and the code has not caught up yet.\n247: \n248: The Hall is the exception and keeps its own depth: fixed ambience gradients, a grain overlay, and an inset highlight on its call to action. That depth is atmospheric rather than structural, and it does not transfer.\n249: \n250: ### Named Rules\n251: \n252: **The Flat Rule.** Depth in the Workroom comes from a hairline or a tonal step. A `box-shadow` on a Workroom surface is a defect.\n253: \n254: **The Two-Step Rule.** Page, then card, then at most one raised step. A surface that needs a fourth level of layering is a surface that needs restructuring.\n255: \n256: ## Shapes\n257: \n258: Corners are gently rounded and consistent: 8px for cards and containers, 6px for buttons and inputs, 4px for the smallest chips and insets, and a full pill only for genuine badges. The scale derives from one 0.5rem radius token, so a change to the base moves the whole system together.\n259: \n260: The Hall uses a near-square 2px radius instead. Its edges are cut, not softened, which is what separates a carved surface from a card.\n261: \n262: Borders are one pixel. There is no second border weight in the Workroom.\n263: \n264: ### Named Rules\n265: \n266: **The Hairline Rule.** One pixel, always. A thicker border used as a coloured accent stripe on the leading edge of a surface is banned, including when faked with an inset shadow. Active state is carried by background tone.\n267: \n268: ## Components\n269: \n270: ### Buttons\n271: \n272: - **Character:** precise and quiet. A button is a plain rectangle with a label. This is the only focus treatment in the Workroom.\n279: - **Hall CTA:** 60px tall, near-square corners, transparent fill over a bronze hairline, with a bronze sheen that sweeps across on hover and a cyan outline on focus.\n280: \n281: ### Cards / Containers\n282: \n283: - **Corner:** 8px.\n284: - **Background:** card white on the page ground.\n285: - **Border:** one-pixel hairline. Do not express focus as a border colour change alone; a border shift is too quiet to serve as the only indicator.\n293: - **Mobile:** 16px text below 768px, so focusing a field never zooms the viewport.\n294: \n295: ### Navigation\n296: \n297: Neutral chrome throughout. Sign-in uses email. Never report a UI change complete on the strength of the diff alone. This is the single biggest recurring failure across past sessions — a hard gate, not a suggestion.\n- **Responsive fixes carry a wider gate: verify across the full emulate matrix BEFORE pushing, not after Joshua reports it.** Narrow, mid, and wide viewports plus the sidecar-docked case, every time. A pushed \"fix\" that does not hold costs a second full session; this has already happened once.\n\n## Workflow Expectations\n\n- Run `npm run build` before wrapping up significant code or documentation work.\n- If tests are relevant to the change, run them too.\n- After completing a change, stage the intended files, commit with a concise message, and push to `origin main` unless the user says otherwise.\n- **Push via `.claude/safe-push.sh`, not raw `git push`.** Lovable auto-commits to `main` mid-session, so a raw push can be rejected or race a concurrent commit. The script fetches, merges `origin/main` if it diverged (never rebases, never force-pushes), then pushes. It also gates on `npm run typecheck`.\n- **Never roll `main` back.** Do not use Lovable's \"Revert to commit\", \"revert and resend\", or history restore, and never reset or force-push `main`. On 2026-09-27 an accidental \"revert and resend\" (b998596) silently undid three merged PRs across 121 question-bank files, and students saw the wrong questions again. To undo your own work, `git revert <your SHA>` only. If a Lovable dialog offers a revert, dismiss it; if one fires, stop and tell Joshua before repairing anything.\n- Existing Codex repo hooks live in `.codex/hooks.json`; preserve them unless the task explicitly requires a hook change.\n\n## Session Protocol (second brain)\n\nProduct context, status, and decisions live in the Obsidian vault at `~/ai-os/`, not this repo. Two repo-local skills in `.agents/skills/` run the session ritual; the canonical protocol is in the vault `CLAUDE.md`.\n\nThe vault was rebuilt 2026-07-16 (paths relative to `~/ai-os`). Read `wiki/tasks.md` (the Now / Next / Done ledger) first, then `wiki/hot.md`, `wiki/dashboard.md`, skim `wiki/index.md`, read the latest `wiki/log.md` entry. Emit a 6-8 line briefing (where we left off, Now, Next, open threads, hot, suggested next) and wait. Do not deep-read other pages until pointed at a task.\n- `wrapup` — end of session. Propose which `## Now` tasks finished and confirm before writing; a wrong \"Done\" is the failure to avoid.
